title: Rainbow Pack / Riley Gantt - Los Angeles City Council Presentation
body: Rainbow Pack / Riley Gantt - Los Angeles City Council Presentation

segments.text: good morning colleagues uh if i could
have everybody's attention we have a a
very special presentation today we're
here to recognize a very very special
young lady and i'm going to get in
trouble with mr labonge because she
actually is a resident of the fourth
council district but let me tell you
colleagues why riley gant is so
incredible and special
miss gant four years ago visited heaven
and elementary school in my district in
pacoima and during her visit at haddon
she heard from many students who talked
about how difficult it was for them to
be able to accomplish basic things like
coloring let alone their homework
and four years ago she understood that
those supplies are incredibly important
to the success of young people and so at
the very very tender age of 10 years old
riley started rainbow pack
a non-profit organization that delivers
non backpacks filled with necessary
homework supplies for students so that
they could actually be successful in
school
ten years old establishes a non-profit
called rainbow pack to make sure that
students have what they need to be
successful at school
since that day riley has helped with her
parents uh brad and leanna
and rainbowpack is certified as a
nonprofit and they have distributed over
two thousand backpacks
to haddon avenue elementary this year
i'm very lucky and very fortunate that
she invited my office to participate to
do two additional elementary schools so
not only are the schools at haddon
elementary and telfair elementary both
in pacquiao going to benefit but sharp
avenue elementary in council district
six ms martinez is always going also
going to have the benefit of having
rainbow pack make these donations and so
i'm very very honored to represent a a
tremendous council district in los
angeles but even more so to have the
partnership of a tremendous individual
a remarkable young lady in riley gantt
who is not just doing things in her
community but she's doing them for mine
and across los angeles today we're also
joined with school board member monica
ratliff who is going to share some words
as well to honor this remarkable young
lady board member thank you
thank you it is a pleasure to be here
today um i just as a teacher for the
last 10 years before getting on the
school board i can tell you firsthand
how important these school supplies and
these backpacks are to our children the
reality is that many of our families
within lausd have to deal with rent
utilities food and basic supplies such
as backpacks and pencils and pen paper
are things that they really cannot
afford we often take
for granted
i think the fact that many of us can
just zip down to target or office depot
and stock up on school supplies for our
children and our students but the
reality is that many of our families
can't this makes such a difference to
the self-esteem of the students when
they are able to walk in on the first
day of school with a backpack and school
supplies so what she has done has
touched the lives of thousands of our
children and it is just remarkable what
she's done i hope that she will also
inspire all of us to do what we can
within our communities to help the
children
who are less fortunate and are unable to
start the day with those things that we
take for granted thank you so much riley
thank you board member ratliff now i'd
like to ask riley to say a few words on
why it is that she's doing this and how
this started riley
why are you doing this
um well i first got introduced to haddon
on a school trip
and i was talking with some of the
students at the table and one of the
little girls said that she wanted a box
of just the basic skinny crayola crayons
but her mom said she couldn't afford
them this was absolutely astonishing to
me this was something that i never had
to deal with as a kid i had more crayons
that i could ever want and to think that
a kid didn't even have the supplies to
do a color by numbers in kindergarten
was really upsetting to me
i went home to my parents and we started
thinking of ways to help originally it
started with just maybe a crayon
collection drive at my school
then we got in contact with the school
social worker randall edwards and she
told us that the problem was much bigger
than just crayons it was backpacks
pencils
any basic school supplies that you could
think of
and so we started trying to think of
ways that we could help our first goal
was just to do one grade the
kindergarten grade hadn't we surpassed
our goal and did first grade and the
pre-k classes
the next year we set a goal to the
entire school
we did that
and the next year we did two schools we
accomplished that this year our goal was
to do a giant back to school event that
would encompass three schools
and would not only give out backpacks
but teach the parents about the
importance of education school and
attendance
and i just want to say thank you so much
this is such a great honor
give her a big round of applause
colleagues
i also want to report and this is
probably when i won't get in trouble for
uh telling somebody's age but riley last
friday turned 14.
so we want to wish her a special happy
birthday and we want to thank her and
commend her on behalf of the city of los
angeles this great city council on what
it is to bring community together and
more importantly to understand when
other folks are in need that neighbors
community members can go to
their aid and help and she's done that
and we're so proud of her mr labonge
congratulations on having a tremendous
family uh in your council district and
let's give her another round of applause
thank you very much
and here's another certificate for your
birthday
all right so let's go to the back
